correctness.rationale: At h≥sqrt(2/3) the eight cap interiors are disjoint and boundary contact is null. Signed permutations preserve both the observation and full-sphere forms. Coordinate-sign parity kills cross terms except same-coordinate B–C terms; swapping the other two coordinates kills those, and permutations give scalar action on the one-, three-, and three-dimensional sectors. The squared norms under probability area are 1/105, 4/105, and 4/7 in the frozen order. On a diagonal cap the azimuthal moment for a coordinate cubic can be computed with x1=a+d cos(phi), a=t/sqrt(3), d²=2(1-t²)/3; the xyz moment follows from the product a³-3ad²/4+(d³/4)cos(3phi) of the three phase-shifted coordinates. The remaining triplet moment follows also from the degree-three addition-theorem identity 105 p_A+(315/4)p_B+(21/4)p_C=7. The cap measure factor is 4 after summing the eight probability-area contributions. Integrating the circle averages reproduces the three branches and trace 28(1-h). The first two difference quadratics in h² are positive on [2/3,1), and 30h⁴-33h²+7 has just one zero there, the stated radical. The top branch remains A; only the B and C triplets tie for the minimum. Nonzero harmonics yield strictly positive energy on each open cap. The leading coefficients at h=1 are 140/9, 140/3 and 112/27 in orders one, two and one respectively; hence the squared condition number is asymptotic to 1/[3(1-h)]. The source verifier was inspected but not executed; separate symbolic recomputation and the exact comparison below corroborate the polynomial and ordering checks. Nothing here extends the formula to overlapping caps or to a low-pass band.

originality.rationale: Demonstrably covered by the 2026-11-08 tetrahedral-cap record f727ebdca345. The eight centers are its four centers together with their antipodes. For any two pure degree-three harmonics f,g, the product conjugate(f)g is even under the antipodal map. At h≥sqrt(2/3) the tetrahedral mask and its antipode are disjoint up to measure zero. Thus the full cube operator is exactly twice the prior tetrahedral operator at the same h, not merely a related symmetry case. On the narrower cubical interval the prior one-dimensional branch is strictly largest, so that triplet zero is automatically a six-dimensional minimum. The same published polynomials give the squared condition number and its endpoint expansion; the factor two cancels in the ratio. The frozen relationship-to-prior-work claim of nonimplication from the tetrahedral result is contradicted by this exact reduction.
